summary: A statement from the IAB and IESG about cryptographic technology, saying that privacy and protection of commercial transactions require wide availability of strong cryptography. It is a best current practice document.

eli5.summary: The people who guide the Internet said that everyone should be able to use strong secret codes to keep their messages and shopping private.

questions: what is the iab statement on cryptography
why should strong cryptography be widely available
why are export controls on encryption bad
subtitle: The IAB and IESG argue against export controls, weak keys and key escrow for cryptography.

tldr.problem: Governments have actual or proposed policies that restrict cryptography, which the IAB and IESG see as harming privacy and commerce on the Internet.
tldr.mechanism: The statement lists four kinds of restrictive policy and then gives a technical analysis of key size, certification authorities, key escrow, signature keys, international conflicts and other points.
tldr.outcome: It concludes that cryptography is the most powerful single tool for securing the Internet, and that knowingly making it weaker has no proven benefit.

facts.label: Policy types opposed
facts.value: 4 (export controls, weak keys, mandated key holding, prohibition)

today: RFC 1984 is a Best Current Practice document according to its metadata, and has not been obsoleted or updated. The text itself is labelled Informational and states a position rather than defining a protocol.

sections.title: The Concern
sections.content:
The Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG) are concerned about the protection of international commercial transactions and about offering all Internet users adequate privacy. Security mechanisms being developed in the IETF depend on the international use of adequate cryptographic technology.

They are disturbed by government policies that (a) impose export controls, (b) restrict users to weak mechanisms such as short keys, (c) mandate that private decryption keys be held by the government or another third party, or (d) prohibit cryptology entirely or permit it only to specially authorized organizations. They encourage policies that allow ready access to uniform strong cryptography for all users in all countries.
sections.eli5: The Internet's guides worry that some countries make it hard to use strong secret codes. They think everyone should be allowed to use good ones.

sections.title: The Claims
sections.content:
The statement claims that the Internet is becoming the predominant vehicle for electronic commerce, so its support structure must be trustworthy. Encryption is not a secret technology monopolized by one country: any hobbyist can program a PC to do powerful encryption, and many algorithms are well documented.

Export controls and usage controls put companies in that country at a competitive disadvantage. Escrow mechanisms inevitably weaken overall security by creating new points of vulnerability that can and will be attacked. These controls slow the deployment of security while attackers become more sophisticated.
sections.eli5: Good secret codes are not a secret anymore, so blocking them mostly hurts honest people and honest companies.

sections.title: Technical Analysis
sections.content:
The analysis has several parts:

  • Key size: restricting use or export by key size is not acceptable, because systems breakable by one country will be breakable by others, and faster computers make today's key sizes insecure later.
  • Public key infrastructure: certification authorities are legitimate and necessary, but they hold public keys and should not be confused with escrow centers, which hold private keys.
  • Keys should not be revealable: secret keys should never leave their user's secure environment, and escrow contradicts that.
  • Data recovery: it should be the customer's choice whether lost keys mean lost data.
  • Signature keys: keys for signatures and authentication must never be escrowed, since a third party could impersonate the owner and non-repudiation would fail.

It adds that conflicting national rules force international companies to use weak encryption, and that escrow does not stop someone from encrypting with another scheme first. It also notes that perfect forward secrecy is generally incompatible with escrow of private keys, calling this an oversimplification of a longer analysis.
sections.eli5: Your secret key is like the only key to your diary. If someone else keeps a copy, the diary is no longer really private, and nobody can be sure who wrote in it.

sections.title: Conclusions and Status
sections.content:
The statement concludes that as more companies and more commerce reach the Internet, security becomes more critical. Cryptography is the most powerful single tool users have, and knowingly making it weaker threatens their ability to secure the Internet and has no proven benefit. The Security Considerations section says security issues are discussed throughout the memo.

RFC 1984 is dated July 24, 1996, and is labelled Informational. It does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.
sections.eli5: The final message is simple. Strong secret codes are the best tool for staying safe online, and making them weaker does not clearly help anyone.
